mockup_note: features/collab-terms-by-aim/04-preview/mockups/collab-terms.html — eight boards drawn from the live screens, with every proposed value traced to a field that exists and is populated in production.

items.1: Sales collab leads with the percentage, not ₹0 — SHIPPED. Second pass 2026-08-25 after the founder showed the LIST still reading ₹0: the fault lived in four places, not one (CollabRow, normalizeRequest, normalizeProposal, and getMyCampaigns never sending commission_pct). The list and the detail page now share one description of the deal.
items.2: Date pickers wherever a date is entered — SHIPPED. Five fields across five screens. Written in JS rather than using the native picker, because nothing in the app imports @react-native-community/datetimepicker so there is no evidence it is in the installed APK, and an OTA cannot add a native module.
items.3: Pay-for-content: one date, a deadline, no window — SHIPPED. Also caught a break it would have caused: handshake.termsFromProposal emitted a window for paid pitches, which the new rule refuses, so ACCEPTING a pay-for-content pitch would have failed validation. Her own pitch screen now offers one date too.
items.4: Deliverables asked of the brand on a fee deal — SHIPPED. Required for engagement/hybrid, allowed but never demanded on conversion. Left OPTIONAL_TERMS: they take no requirement marker and are always negotiable on a paid deal. Vocabulary reused from contracts; duplicates and zero counts refused.
items.5: Deliverables not asked of the creator on a sales deal — SHIPPED. Also repairs a break item 4 introduced: her counter attached importance:{deliverables:preference}, which item 4 now refuses, so every counter touching deliverables would have failed validation. Her form is now paid-only, uses all five formats, and pre-fills from the brand request so countering the money does not wipe agreed deliverables.
items.6: Where she works becomes negotiable, loses requirement/preference — SHIPPED. Now required and always counterable on both aims. Legacy markers TOLERATED rather than refused: unlike deliverables, all 14 live requests carried one, so refusing would have broken every live conversation on the next counter. Also caught a regression: her screen only rendered the working style when a marker was present, so new markerless requests would have shown her none at all.
items.7: Counter in place, beside each term, with a change count — SHIPPED. The separate second copy of the offer is gone. Controls pre-fill from the brand offer so no-change is the default; the comparison lives in utils/collabCounter with 14 tests because it decides what travels.
items.8: Specific products as a scope option — SHIPPED. The model already accepted the shape; only the brand had no picker. Names travel with the ids so an agreement still reads properly after a product is renamed or removed.
items.9: Category from the listing tree, not typed — SHIPPED. Two findings: (a) I built a duplicate GET /brands/me/listing-tree and only discovered on the live probe that a better one already existed, annotated with per-category product counts — mine was shadowed, never ran, and is deleted; (b) the brand-to-vertical resolver was case-sensitive and existed in TWO copies, so any brand carrying a capitalised category (Kanchi Silks, 11 products) got an EMPTY tree. Now one copy in utils/vertical.
items.10: Pitch settings moved — SHIPPED 2026-08-25 under stage-1
items.11: One ask template, three ways in — SHIPPED. Founder found that asking a group opened a different screen. It was worse than cosmetic: two composers existed, this batch upgraded one, and items 4 and 6 broke the other outright — asking a group or a filtered set could not send at all, proven against production. BrandAskManyScreen deleted; the one composer takes an individual, a group or a filter. The bulk reach preview and the skipped-reasons result page were carried over, not lost.

deferred: Constraining her post to the agreed category — a posting rule, not a collaboration screen. Now UNBLOCKED: the agreement carries a real category_node_id for the first time.

release.deploy_class: production-impacting (creator app via OTA). Item 1 has no backend change and no migration.
release.qa_note:
2026-08-25 — item 1. Mobile 178/178 (was 159 before this contract; 14 money checks plus 5 list-level checks added). Android bundle builds. The shipped list query verified against production: four sales campaigns carry 18/15/20/22 and two content campaigns carry ₹30,000 and ₹25,000.
  Backend change is one SELECT list (commission_pct, influencer_budget) on the creator campaigns list. No migration.
  NOT CLAIMED GREEN — the full serial backend suite has not been runnable since 2026-08-22.
  ITEM 3 — 12 assertions run directly against collabTerms.model (jest globalSetup connects to the test DB before any suite runs, so no suite can execute while it is down). tests/collab-terms-time.test.js is written and waiting. Mobile 188/188. Bundle builds. No migration: all 14 live requests and 8 agreements already carry post_by and none carries a window.

regression_found_2026_08_25: CollabRow still switched on the PRE-Stage-1 stage names, so every row fell through to its default: the hint read "Archived" on unanswered invitations, the badge showed a raw status instead of whose turn it is, and the expiry countdown and delivered count had never once rendered. The smoke test stayed green by asserting five stage names the app had stopped producing. Fixed, and the test now guards that the stages it uses equal COLLAB_STAGES.
all_items_shipped: 1-10 all shipped 2026-08-25. Deferred: constraining her post to the agreed category — now UNBLOCKED, since an agreement carries a real category_node_id for the first time.
recurring_fault: Third time in a fortnight: two creator search screens, two listing-tree endpoints, two ask composers. Each time one copy received changes the other did not. The api layer had even documented the intent — "the same composer, three ways in" — months before two screens were built anyway.
